title: The Focused Beam
cue: One task. Ten minutes. Begin.
explanation: The bloom has many layers and one centre. Let the centre stand for the one task you choose next.
action: Pick one useful task. Work on it for ten minutes. Each time you drift, return to that task.

title: The Space Between
cue: Pause. Exhale. Choose.
explanation: The space inside the arches is part of the design. Let it remind you to leave a small pause before choosing.
action: Before one reactive reply today, pause, let out a gentle breath, and choose what to say.

title: Intentional Unlock
cue: When I unlock, I choose my purpose.
explanation: The sun is a cue to wake up to what you are doing. When the screen lights up, choose why you are opening it.
action: Before opening an app, say why you unlocked your phone. If there is no purpose, put it down.

title: The First Two Minutes
cue: Make the first step small enough to start.
explanation: Each flowing line begins with a small movement. You can start a task with a step that takes only two minutes.
action: Choose a task you have avoided. Do its smallest first step for two minutes.

title: Thought Is Not Fact
cue: Notice the thought. Check the evidence.
explanation: The rings spread outward from one point. A thought can expand quickly too; return to what the evidence actually supports.
action: Write down a troubling thought. Identify a fact that supports it and a fact that complicates it.

title: Return to Now
cue: Feel your feet. Notice what is here.
explanation: The quiet moon is a cue to notice the place you are in. Start with your feet and one ordinary detail around you.
action: At three natural pauses, feel your feet and name three things you can see.

title: Name the Feeling
cue: Name it before you act.
explanation: The bloom holds different layers together. You can name a feeling without making it the whole of who you are.
action: Name a strong feeling in plain words. Then choose one useful next action.

title: The Slow Exhale
cue: Let the next exhale be gentle and unhurried.
explanation: The repeating arches create space and rhythm. Use the image to remember an easy, unforced exhale.
action: Take three comfortable breaths with unhurried exhales. Return to normal breathing if uncomfortable.

title: One Next Action
cue: Write the next action. Do only that.
explanation: The sun has one centre among many rays. Choose a single next action from the many things you could do.
action: Write one action beginning with a verb. Do that action before planning the rest.

title: Close the Loop
cue: Choose a finish line. Reach it.
explanation: The flowing lines have a visible path. Give your task a clear stopping point so you can notice when it is done.
action: Define what finished means for one small task. Complete that version before adding more.

title: Active Recall
cue: Close the page. Recall one idea.
explanation: The rings are a reminder to bring an idea back to mind. Try recalling it before looking at the page again.
action: After studying, close the page and explain one idea from memory. Reopen it to check.

title: Space the Practice
cue: Review tomorrow. Return next week.
explanation: The moon suggests returning rather than rushing. Revisit what you are learning after a gap.
action: Review one idea today. Schedule a short review for tomorrow and next week.

title: Learn from Error
cue: Find the error. Change one step.
explanation: A bloom is made of many small parts. One imperfect part can show you what to adjust next.
action: Identify a step that led to one mistake. Change that step and try again.

title: Protect Your Attention
cue: Silence one distraction before you begin.
explanation: The arches frame an open space. Protect a little space for the task you want to give your attention to.
action: Silence one notification source and move one distraction out of reach before focusing.

title: Rest Is a Rhythm
cue: Choose a bedtime. Begin winding down.
explanation: The sun marks a daily rhythm. Let the reminder cue a consistent evening wind-down that suits your life.
action: Choose tonight's wind-down time. Dim your environment and stop one stimulating activity then.

title: Move the Body
cue: Stand up. Take a short walk.
explanation: The flowing lines suggest motion. Use them as a cue to change position or take a comfortable movement break.
action: Take a short comfortable walk at a natural break, or choose movement suitable for your body.

title: The Kinder Voice
cue: Speak to yourself as you would to a friend.
explanation: The rings spread from the centre. A kinder response to yourself can begin with one ordinary sentence.
action: Rewrite a self-critical sentence as advice you would give a friend. Use that advice.

title: Compare Less
cue: Choose your own next step.
explanation: The moon keeps its own place in the design. Return to the next step that fits your own circumstances.
action: When comparison distracts you, take one step toward your own goal.

title: The Worry Window
cue: Write the worry. Choose when to revisit it.
explanation: The layered bloom gives your eyes a centre to return to. Put a worry somewhere you can revisit at a chosen time.
action: Write a non-urgent worry down and schedule ten minutes to revisit it. Handle urgent practical issues now.

title: Make Room
cue: Let the feeling be here. Choose your action.
explanation: The open arch leaves room for what is there. A feeling can be present while you choose a useful action.
action: Notice a difficult feeling without demanding it disappear. Take a small action that matters to you.

title: Check the Story
cue: What happened? What am I adding?
explanation: The sun draws a clear centre. Start with what happened, then notice the interpretation you added.
action: Describe an upsetting event using observable facts. Write your interpretation separately.

title: Control the Next Step
cue: Act on what is yours to change.
explanation: The flowing lines suggest a direction, not a destination. Choose the next step that is actually yours to take.
action: List one thing you can influence. Spend ten minutes acting on it.

title: Respond with Care
cue: Read again. Reply after a pause.
explanation: The rings suggest how a response can travel outward. Pause long enough to choose a reply you can stand behind.
action: Reread a tense message after a pause. Make one edit that improves clarity or care.

title: Listen First
cue: Understand before you answer.
explanation: The quiet moon is a cue to leave room in the conversation. Let the other person finish before preparing your reply.
action: Summarise what you heard and check your understanding before giving advice in one conversation.

title: Set the Boundary
cue: Say what you can do. Say what you cannot.
explanation: The bloom has a defined shape. A clear boundary can also make room for a relationship to work.
action: Use a clear sentence: I can do this, but I cannot do that. Offer a realistic alternative if helpful.

title: Notice the Good
cue: Name one specific thing you appreciate.
explanation: The arches frame a small opening. Notice one specific good thing instead of trying to make the whole day feel different.
action: Name one thing you appreciate and why. If it involves someone, consider telling them yourself.

title: Repeat the Cue
cue: After my daily cue, I do one small action.
explanation: The sun is an ordinary repeating cue. Pair an existing daily moment with one small helpful action.
action: Make a plan: After [daily routine], I will [small action]. Practise it at that cue today.

title: Change the Environment
cue: Put the helpful choice within reach.
explanation: The lines flow along a prepared path. Arrange your surroundings so the helpful action is easier to begin.
action: Put a useful object where you will use it: a book, walking shoes, or a water bottle.

title: Begin Again
cue: A missed day is a cue to return.
explanation: The rings always offer a centre to return to. After a missed day, begin with the next small action.
action: Resume a paused habit with its smallest useful version. Return without trying to catch up.

title: Practise the Person
cue: Choose one action that matches your values.
explanation: The moon offers a quiet point of orientation. Choose an ordinary action that expresses a value you care about.
action: Choose a value such as care, learning, or honesty. Take one concrete action that expresses it.
